entry.dc:title: Opencast contracts a consultant's view
entry.dc:creator: Walton G.
entry.dc:description: Contractual claims on opencast sites are inherent in the risk attached to the operations. To resolve such problems, several issues need to be explored, in particular the risk areas in opencast mining. The risk areas may be divided into geological constraints, geotechnical constraints, operational constraints, timing, changes in requirements, environmental restrictions and market.

entry.dc:title: Model for Kovin lignite deposit suction cutterwheel dredging
entry.dc:creator: Pavlović V.
entry.prism:publicationName: Prace Naukowe Instytutu Gornictwa Politechniki Wroclawskiej
entry.dc:description: The Model for suction cutterwheel dredger Kovin UCW-450 operation was developed as programming support for operation of the suction cutterwheel dredger engaged in lignite deposit "Kovin" in Kovin. In its structure the model represents an integral parts of a research program at the Department for Opencast Mining of University of Belgrade Faculty of Mining and Geology in the areas of working out mathematical models of mineral material deposits and modelling of technological processes and procedures of opencast mining systems. The Model was developed as an application for lignite deposit "Kovin" concrete conditions as support in optimization of operation technological parameters and course of dredger advance during dredging.

entry.dc:title: From wasteland to wonderland: Opencast mining, regeneration and the English National Forest
entry.dc:creator: Cloke P.
entry.dc:description: In this paper we examine the outcomes of restructuring within the British coal mining industry in the English countryside and an attempt by the Countryside Commission to regenerate an area of the rural East Midlands through a forest project of sustainable development. In this particular area, deep-mine coal production has collapsed resulting in high levels of unemployment and large parcels of derelict land, while an expansion of opencast coal (and other mineral) extraction has led to considerable landscape despoliation. We examine critically the Countryside Commission's project of the National Forest in this area, involving the planting of thirty million trees over an area of almost 200 square miles. The Forest is seen as an example of sustainable development, bringing together economic growth - based around timber production and the encouragement of tourism and 'green' business -and environmental enhancement. However, the National Forest will be planted on private land, some of which is controlled by major mineral companies, with relatively little public ownership of this so-called 'national asset'. The paper draws on recent research carried out by the authors which has explored a series of important land use conflicts surrounding the sustainability of the Forest alongside on-going processes of opencast mining within its boundaries and also tensions associated with public access within a privately-owned forest. entry.dc:title: Evaluation of land use potential for quarrying area around Ramganjmandi (Kota, Rajasthan), India
entry.dc:creator: Sharma D.K.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
entry.dc:description: Large opencast mining leads to problems of land degradation and calls for quarry planning, particularly reclamation and post-quarried land use aspect of secondary utilisation mined out areas effectively. The problem becomes more complex as quarrying operations approach more densely populated areas and forest areas. The aim of the present study is to outline appropriate potential, secondary use for quarried land for which two approaches, first based on logical study of natural and cultural parameter, and second approach is computer-aided and uses a model to decide the priorities for the best suited quarried land uses. A case study of Satalkhedi Laxmipura area in Ramganjmandi, Kota (Rajasthan), India, has been presented.

entry.dc:title: Effects of topsoiling on rates of erosion and erosion processes in coal mine spoil banks in Utrillas, Teruel, Spain
entry.dc:creator: Nicolau J.M.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
entry.dc:description: Runoff production and soil erosion, produced by energetic Mediterranean storms, are amongst the first environmental impacts of opencast mining activity and amongst the main limiting factors in achieving self-sustaining reclaimed landscapes in Teruel. This paper aims to understand the geomorphological response of topsoiled and overburden-covered banks. This is considered essential in improving soil management and designing accurate erosion control plans. Runoff and erosion rates were recorded after every rainfall in permanent plots for one year in both overburden and topsoiled banks. In the same way experiments were conducted with a portable rainfall simulator to follow the response evolution throughout time. Grass communties control topsoiled bank evolution, leading to an improvement in the hydric characteristics of the topsoil during ecological succession. Physical-chemical soil properties condition the erosion processes in overburden-covered banks. No improvement in infiltration rate nor in erodibility has been recorded 6 years after the slope banks were constructed.

entry.dc:title: Restoration of the Ackton opencast coal site, West Yorkshire
entry.dc:description: This short article describes the restoration of a site which was scarred by spoil heaps from underground mining and from subsequent opencast mining operations. The reinstatement of the site resulted in a prestigious environmental award for Miller Mining. -Author

entry.dc:title: The prediction of opencast backfill settlement
entry.dc:creator: Hills C.W.W.
entry.prism:publicationName: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers Geotechnical Engineering
entry.dc:description: With ever-increasing demands on land use, large areas of land are being considered for development, which owing to past mining activities are covered by substantial depths of fill materials. This paper examines the problem faced, with the development of land infilled with opencast mining backfill, in predicting the behaviour of the fill upon development. To be able to design foundations suitable to withstand the movements that occur within opencast backfill or to design a backfilling operation that produces land suitable for development, a means of predicting backfill settlement is required. The information required to make accurate predictions includes the timing of backfilling operations, the compactive state and type of backfill, and the inundation of the backfill. This information will be available in most cases where development is planned, as a scheme of controlled backfilling will generally be undertaken. The resultant monitoring scheme, carried out to ensure controls are being met during backfilling, will provide the information necessary to enable settlement predictions to be made. From the analysis of a considerable quantity of data collected from the monitoring of backfilling operations and backfill movement at a range of opencast coal sites located within the UK, a computer program has been developed, enabling opencast backfill settlement predictions to be made taking into consideration the factors mentioned above. To demonstrate the validity of the approach, a case study is carried out from a real site from which a comparison between predicted and actual settlements can be made.

entry.dc:title: Environmental dust analysis in opencast mining areas
entry.dc:creator: Merefield J.
entry.dc:description: An atmospheric dust database has been set up for the western end of the South Wales Coalfield. This, the first of its kind in the UK, comprises dust data from British Standard 1747 four-way directional gauges, a window ledge sampler and an experimental frisbee deposit gauge. X-Ray diffraction was used to characterize the dust on the basis of mineralogy. Scanning electron microscopy was used to examine particle size and shape and an energy dispersive X-ray analysis system was used to locate coal particles. For 18 months, a total of 15 directional and three frisbee gauges were used to collect dust on and around the Ffos Las opencast coal site in South Wales, UK. Additionally, two more directional gauges have been installed in the Brecon Beacons and at Exeter in south-west England to provide data from outside the coal mining area. Processed data from the X-ray diffractograms, along with the weather data from an onsite weather gauge, are input to a geographical information system (ArcInfo), where they can be manipulated statistically. Rose diagram plots for the area can thus be presented, giving the mineralogical contents of dust from the four directions of each sampling station, set in a spatial context. A series of these plots introduces the temporal element. This new dust data technology already shows considerable potential for use in nuisance complaints, planning applications, site licence renewals and for the implementation of future European environmental protection legislation. © 1995 The Geological Society.

entry.dc:title: Influence of geological structures in slope stability analyses for opencast mining and quarry excavations
entry.dc:creator: Cojean R.
entry.prism:publicationName: Geological Society Engineering Geology Special Publication
entry.dc:description: The influence of structural features on slope stability in rock masses is analysed, with particular reference to opencast mining and quarrying. Various failure mechanisms are illustrated at different scales. The primary importance of the method of modelling rock masses is highlighted, with discussion about the need to emphasize either the continuous or discontinuous properties of the rock masses. The choice of mechanical parameters for the joints, as well as the rock material, is significant and a slight variation may alter the mode of failure of the slope. There is therefore a need for further investigation into the geological description and mechanical analysis of rock masses. In many instances, sound judgement by an experienced engineering geologist is required to identify the relevant features of the rock mass and to assess the mechanical behaviour that may operate.

entry.dc:title: Opencast mining in Coal India Ltd
entry.dc:creator: Mishra R.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: Coal India Limited has vigorously pursued and succeeded in adopting and absorbing state-of-the-art technologies in opencast mines. Shovel dumper system remains the main technology although a few open pits use walking draglines for stripping operations. Electric rope shovels up to 20 cu.m. bucket capacity are working successfully with standard thyristor control while a wide range of hydraulic excavators are proving their worth in selective mining and medium hard strata conditions.

entry.dc:title: Flora and vegetation on dumps of uranium mining in the southern part of the former GDR
entry.dc:creator: Sanger H.
entry.dc:description: From 1946 to 1990 an intensive uranium mining had been carried out with underground mining and also with opencast mining by the Wismut enterprise in the southern pan of the former GDR. The mining activity lead also in the surroundings of Ronneburg to a permanent growth of devastated areas, among others in the form of dumps and tailings. These areas form by reason of mining-specific contaminations, extrem biotops which demand high claims on the pioneer organisms during the phase of natural first settlement. From 1990 to 1992 vegetation mappings were carried out on 15 dumps of the Thuringia mining area according to Braun-Blanquet (1964). The utilization of the computer prograrnm Flora D (Frank and Klotz 1990) enabled the ecological characterisation of the dumps. On the 15 investigated dumps found were 498 higher plants, belonging to 65 families. One hundred species are species with a high dominance. The number of species per dump fluctuates between 11 and 282. Pioneer plants occur on the berms mostly in the second year after stoppage of the dumping, on the slopes after five to ten years. After nearly ten years the first step of settlement seems to be finished. Among the mechanisms of spreading dominate wind-And burdock spread. According to the form of life forms the dump species are predominantly henlicryptop- hytes, further therophytes, geophytes and phanerophytes.

The genus Succinosciara MOH. & RÖSCH. gen. nov. with the typespecies Succinosciara acuminata spec. nov., the subgenus Protolycoriella MOH. & RÖSCH. subgen. nov. with Lycoriella (Protolycoriella) gigaspina spec. nov. as the typespecies and additional 12 new species are described and drawn. 14 of the species from Saxonian amber are also known from Baltic amber. entry.dc:title: Cainozoic of the Konin area with special emphasis on the stratigraphy of Quaternary deposits
entry.dc:creator: Stankowski W.
entry.dc:description: A characteristic geological feture of the Konin region is the shallow occurrence of the Mesozoic rocks. The palaeorelief is marked by vast, valley-type depresions of erosional origin, as well as by grabens. Tectonic activity took place in that area not only in the Tertiary but also during the Quaternary period. Thick Tertiary series were deposited during the period between the Eocene and the Miocene. Within the Quaternary sediments, series of three cold periods have been distinguished: the South Polish Glaciation, the Middle Polish Glaciation and the North Polish Glaciation. Similarly, series of two warm periods, those of the Great Interglacial and of the Eemian Interglacial have been encountered. Rapid transformations in the relief, as well as in the geological structure and water conditions, have been the result of Tertiary coal opencast mining. -from Authors

entry.dc:title: Polish lignite mine provides major source of power
entry.dc:description: This short feature describes the Belchatow opencast mining operation in Poland. The pit supplies coal for a 4320 MW power plant which produces 20% of the country's energy. -Author

entry.dc:title: Prediction of subsoil subsidence caused by opencast mining
entry.dc:creator: Konderla H.
entry.prism:publicationName: Land Subsidence Proc International Symposium the Hague 1995
entry.dc:description: Attempts were made to formulate the correlation between the subsidence of the soil mass exposed to opencast mining and the parameters characterizing the development of the depression and the geological structure of the seam. The process of soil surface subsidence was analysed, making use of the results from geodetic and piezometric measurements carried out in one of Poland's brown-coal mines. A simple model was proposed for the prediction of superficial displacements produced by the dewatering of the soil mass. The subsidence and rise of the soil surface, recorded in the course of geodetic measurements, reflect both the effect of seam dewatering and the effect of mining operations. -from Authors

entry.dc:title: Soil factors affecting tree growth on former opencast coal land
entry.dc:creator: Scullion J.
entry.dc:description: The growth of three tree species (Alnus glutinosa, Betula spp. and Quercus spp.) was related to soil factors on two restored opencast coal sites in South Wales, UK. The main factors favouring tree growth were greater soil depth and organic content. Factors limiting growth included poor site drainage and high magnesium levels. Whilst all species were related to most of the above factors, soil depth was of particular importance for Alnus glutinosa and Betula spp., whilst site drainage had the greatest influence for Betula spp. Soil‐tree associations tended to be closer on the older of the two sites. Combinations of soil depth, percentage clay and percentage organic content in a multiple regression predicted around 40 per cent of the growth variation in Alnus glutinosa, between 6.9 and 32 per cent of that for Betula spp. and between 14.5 and 32.6 per cent of that for Quercus spp. Growth prediction for Betula spp. improved to 40.9 and 34.8 per cent when a site drainage factor was included in the regression. The development of such predictive relationships might contribute to the planning of site reinstatement for tree planting after opencast mining, and to a better ‘matching’ of tree species to site characteristics. entry.dc:title: Engineering geomorphological mapping and opencast mining in unstable mountains - a case study
entry.dc:creator: Hearn G.
entry.prism:publicationName: Transactions Institution of Mining Metallurgy Section A
entry.dc:description: The application and value of rapid geomorphological mapping techniques in the assessment of slope instability and erosion hazards in the remote and mountainous area of Ok Tedi mine, Papua New Guinea, are reviewed. It is believed that this mapping is the first to have been systematically applied to any mining operation in remote mountainous terrain. Rock avalanches and landslides are features of the area around the mine and represent potential hazards to mine operations. In 1989 an avalanche with an estimated volume of 70 000 000 m<sup>3</sup> occurred in close proximity to the mine and promoted a multidisciplinary geotechnical study of the entire mine operational area. The assessment of landslide hazard and geomorphological mapping formed integral parts of the study and were carried out at rates of 0.6-0.75 km<sup>2</sup> per week. They yielded various documentation for geotechnical management. This documentation, together with the conclusions reached and recommendations made, played an important role in the geotechnical assessment of slopes in the mine operational area. -from Author

entry.dc:title: Monitoring airborne dust from quarrying and surface mining operations
entry.dc:creator: Merefield J.R.
entry.prism:publicationName: Transactions Institution of Mining Metallurgy Section A
entry.dc:description: This note introduces the concept of "finger-printing' airborne dust samples on the basis of mineralogy by providing information on ambient dust levels before opencast mining and quarrying operations and a dynamic record during them. The intention is to provide site operators and regulators with the means to eliminate dust nuisance from disputes over planning and licence applications before it becomes a serious hazard. -Authors

entry.dc:title: Mineralogy and provenance of airborne dust in opencast coal mining areas of South Wales
entry.dc:creator: Merefield J.R.
entry.dc:description: Fugitive dust from opencast mining is a contentious issue. It has often been perceived to be a significant contributor to ambient levels of airborne particulates, even though no reliable means of dust fingerprinting has been available to regulatory authorities. To address this need, dust has been collected continuously for an eighteen month period in and around Ffos Las opencast coal mine in South Wales, over an area covering some 250 square kilometres. Samples have been analysed for mineral content by X-ray diffraction (XRD), and particle shape, size and geochemistry by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with EDAX energy dispersive X-ray analysis. By this means it has proven possible for the first time to fingerprint dust from different sources, such as on-site and immediately off-site of the opencast coal workings, and elsewhere in the region. The results show calcite and dolomite to occur over the entire study area, indicating a significant regional component present in airborne dust in the Ffos Las locality. Local sources are recognised by an increase in clay minerals such as chlorite and kaolinite over non-clay minerals such as quartz. Chlorite being detected on-site and occasionally near-site, characterises dust derived from Ffos Las opencast coal workings. Local dust generation, however, is not restricted to Ffos Las opencast site. Dust arising from quarrying, road developments and ground cover in residential properties can make a substantial contribution to the dust flux in this area. This new dust data technology has proven particularly effective and will be of considerable use in the implementation of future environmental protection legislation in Europe and world-wide.

entry.dc:title: Mining simulation of a new type continuous surface miner
entry.dc:creator: Xichun X.
entry.dc:description: A new type of continuous surface coal miner (csm) and mining simulation tests carried out for designing it are introduced in this paper. The tests provided a reliable basis for determining the main technical parameters and the structure of the new machine. Emphasis was put on the test rig, the coal and rock mass specimens, and the system and contents of test and data processing. The continuous surface miner is a new type of opencast mining equipment. In order to determine the technical parameters and basic structure of its working device, we have carried out a series of cutting and loading experiments upon the drum with various parameters of helical vane and pick arrangement in rock and coal specimens of different height on a mining simulation test rig, and measured seven parameters. The results of this project have been adopted in the design of this machine.

entry.dc:title: High-power inverters optimize mammoth excavator
entry.dc:creator: O'Connor R.
entry.dc:description: Inverters are used to optimize the performance of excavators used in digging coal at opencast mining sites. The dc technology controlling the travel-and boom-slewing motions of such excavator lacks the fine control necessary to provide maximum output when the excavator is operating on variable terrain. With respect to this problem, a new system that improves performance and reduce downtime is used. The use of SIMOVERT P inverters that combines the V/F method and vector control technique showed a promising performance. The control of these inverters is fully digitized. This system is specifically integrated to the No. 292 excavator.

entry.dc:title: Opencast operations at Optimum Colliery, South Africa
entry.dc:creator: Rutten O.
entry.dc:description: The Optimum Colliery is one of South Africa's major opencast coal mining operation under the Division of the Trans-Natal Coal Corporation, Limited. The coal were initially mined using underground mining procedures. However, due to the proven success of an opencast mining enterprise, the entire production at Optimum Colliery was altered to opencast extraction. Four walking draglines consisting of Marion models 8000, 8200-12A, 195 and 7450 were employed for stripping. Three rope shovels and four wheel loaders as well as 12 bottom-dump coal haulers and five rear-dump trucks were used for coal loading and hauling.

entry.dc:title: Opencast mining for coal in the People's Republic of China
entry.dc:creator: Zhang Y.
entry.dc:description: The opencast coal mining in the People's Republic of China (PRC) has shown the benefits of this method of mining over conservative underground mining. Opencast mining provide high production, shorter construction terms, minimal cost, increased labor productivity, lesser unit investment, higher coal recovery and enhanced working conditions and better safety record. However, there are many consideration that must be taken into account when applying opencast mining technique in the PRC. These include ground water resources and human resources, which are particularly significant factors in remote areas such as the Inner Mongolian Autonomous Region.

entry.dc:title: Mining and the environment - an agenda for action
entry.dc:creator: De P.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: The phenomenon of environmental and ecological damage has been threatening the country more and more by every passing day, substantiated as it is by the late or non-arrival of the monsoon. This paper seeks to point the major areas of concern in terms of the immediate and the long term fall outs of the mining at a place - be it an underground or an opencast mining activity-and suggest some effective and practically implementable remedial measure. What is being tried to be outlined in this paper is an immediate agenda for action that shall help unite development to environmental safeguards by practically sound and technologically feasible management of natural resources.
